prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states, which opened the field of moire quantum materials.

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep B028 alone as the whole prize, with Bistritzer, MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero. The scientific case has not weakened under scrutiny. No member disputes that the flat-band prediction and the observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states are real and reproduced, and the chair's summary records that several of us would word the citation around flat bands and correlated phases rather than the pairing mechanism. That wording answers the chair's question on prematurity: the prize would rest on two reproducible facts, a quantitative prediction in 2011 of a bandwidth collapse at a specific angle, and the 2018 observation of gate-tunable correlated states at that angle. The consequence is a new control knob for correlated-electron physics, set by angle and gating instead of chemistry, which many groups in many materials have since used. The credit maps cleanly onto prediction and observation. Of the other proposals I find B022 the strongest rival on quality and attribution, and I treat it as my first alternative, but I do not think its remaining payoffs (redefinition of the second, constants tests) outweigh what B028 has already changed in condensed-matter research.
statement.case_against: The origin of the superconductivity and of the correlated insulators is unresolved, the field is under a decade old, and the experimental credit leaves out Yuan Cao and the first-author team as well as the Dean and Young groups. Several colleagues (Danielsson, Kroll, Olsson, Johansson) regard the maturity risk as real, and I do not dismiss it. Including Bistritzer uses all three names on a single prize. I also hold myself to the same maturity standard I applied to B001, whose interface mechanism is still debated, and the difference is only that the twisted-graphene phenomena are better reproduced and better controlled. If the committee judges that a prize should wait until the interpretation stabilises, B022 is the better choice this year, and B048 is my preferred condensed-matter fallback.

responses.point: Kroll keeps B022 first for a clean two-name allocation and independent reproduction, lists B028 as his first alternative, and says he would revisit it if the interpretation of the superconductivity has stabilised.
responses.response: I think the interpretation question is the wrong test, because the claim being honoured does not depend on the pairing mechanism. What must be stable is the existence of the flat-band regime and the reproducible correlated phases, and those are established across independent groups. I agree with you that B022 is cleaner on attribution, and your own list of uncredited contributors (Lemonde, Ludlow, Takamoto and the ion-clock groups) shows that its credit is not airtight either. I still cannot judge the clock's fundamental-physics reach from my own field, so I defer to you and Lindroth on that, but I note that you and Lindroth both place the redefinition of the second ahead of the demonstrated consequences, which is the same kind of prospective argument you apply against B028.

responses.point: Danielsson now prefers a two-part prize of B002 (Halzen) and B022 (Katori and Ye), keeps B028 as an alternative, and would wait for the interpretation of the superconductivity to stabilise.
responses.response: I understand the preference for two clean achievements, but I do not think the pairing is as clean as it looks. Your own and Pearce's statements concede that a one-name prize for IceCube rests on a conceiver-and-leader principle that Kroll and Lindroth explicitly doubt, and that AMANDA-era figures stay outside it. A prize built on a credit principle the committee has not agreed is more fragile than one whose credit is a prediction paired with an observation. On waiting: the 2018 experiments are now reproduced by many groups, and waiting for the pairing mechanism could take much longer than the committee should defer a discovery whose existence is not in doubt. I have not changed my configuration on this point.

responses.point: Mehlig prefers B028 alone for the same three names and acknowledges that the boundary between the founding discovery and the later moire work is not sharp.
responses.response: I agree with the three-name configuration and with your concern about the boundary. I would handle it in the citation by restricting it to the prediction of flat bands at a magic angle and the discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states, and leave fractional Chern insulators and other moire families to the field. That keeps the prize from fixing a narrative the field is still revising, which is your worry, while leaving the credit attached to the dated, falsifiable steps of 2011 and 2018. On Bistritzer, I think his name is justified because the continuum model with its magic-angle prediction is his paper with MacDonald and the experiment tested that specific prediction.

responses.point: Pearce asked me whether the three names for B018 are defensible or whether the conceptual step belongs elsewhere, and states that his B002 and B022 pairing depends on Halzen alone being able to carry a part of the prize.
responses.response: On B018 my answer is that I do not think the three names are defensible as supplied. The infinite-dimension limit (Metzner and Vollhardt) and the impurity-model mapping (Georges and Kotliar, with Rozenberg) were different steps, and the supplied credit omits Metzner and Rozenberg. That is why I no longer put B018 in my configuration, and I keep it only as a distant alternative. On your configuration, you describe the dependence on B002 carrying a part by itself yourself. If the committee does not accept that principle, you say B037 or B028 is the better partner for B022, and I would say that B028 is the better of the two because its credit does not need a collaboration-size principle.

responses.point: Olsson prefers B028 alone with the same three names, lists B031 and B022 as alternatives, and notes that a second condensed-matter materials prize could be avoided in a year when atomic or particle candidates are strong.
responses.response: I agree on the configuration and on the three names. On your worry about condensed-matter concentration, I see it differently. B028 is the only candidate where the committee would be recognising a prediction and its test, and the subfield label should not decide the matter. I also agree with you that B031 mixes two discoveries and I accept that B048 is a narrower and more defensible topological alternative, though still short of B028 for me because Mele, Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang tangle its credit. Your comment that device-to-device variation limits universality is fair and should be reflected in careful wording of the citation, not in delay.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts that a platform discovery with an unsettled superconducting mechanism is mature enough, which is the main reason B022 remains my first alternative.
Whether Bistritzer should be a laureate alongside MacDonald, or whether MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero alone is the stronger configuration.
How Yuan Cao and the other first authors, and the Dean and Young groups, can be acknowledged given the three-person limit.
I cannot independently judge whether the fundamental-physics reach of the optical lattice clock is demonstrated or prospective, and I rely on Kroll and Lindroth for that.
statement.conflict_note: No documented personal or institutional conflict with Bistritzer, MacDonald or Jarillo-Herrero or with the other credited names. My field (electronic-structure theory, DFT and correlated electrons) is close to B028, B048 and B018, which is intellectual proximity and not a relationship with any credited person. I update my disclosure only to say that my vote for B028 does not rest on any claim that my own methods bear on the credited work.
